Research Context
Bio-interfaces are contact zones where diverse cellular activities occur through dynamic biomacromolecules. Extracellular matrix is a key bio-interface that regulates cellular functions via ligand-receptor interactions. Phospholipid bilayers are essential for substance transportation and signal transduction. Membrane deformation regulates bidirectional substance transportation through exocytosis and endocytosis. Supramolecular chemistry and nanotechnology enable construction of dynamic bio-interfaces. Mimicking dynamic bio-interfaces can enable biomaterials for regenerative medicine and drug delivery.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether self-assembling materials can mimic dynamic bio-interfaces for biomedical applications. The hypothesis is that stiffness-controlled peptide hydrogels can enhance neuronal migration after brain injury. The hypothesis is that peptide fibres can incorporate and release growth factors for neural tissue regeneration. The hypothesis is that redox-responsive peptides can control cargo release kinetics. The hypothesis is that stabilized phospholipid nanosheets enable extended blood circulation. The hypothesis is that a membrane-expanding molecular machine enables endocytosis-like fission for virus delivery.

Methodological Details
The article reviews recent studies of bioinspired supramolecular materials mimicking dynamic bio-interfaces. The review highlights artificial extracellular matrices and membrane-deforming supramolecular materials. Self-assembling peptide fibres are recognized as versatile supramolecular scaffolds of biomaterials. Peptide amphiphiles construct nanofibres by forming cylindrical micelles. Diphenylalanine has been extensively studied as a backbone to afford supramolecular fibres. RADA16 peptides form supramolecular nanofibres through beta-sheet hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interaction. RADA-based peptides can be used as a tag sequence incorporated into proteins of interest with an E. coli expression system. Peptide fibre dynamics can be tuned by amino acid sequences, particularly in the hydrophobic part. Conformational flexibility of peptide fibres can be a critical factor in controlling the stiffness of the hydrogels. Glycine residues generally enhance the conformational flexibility of polypeptide chains. The mammalian brain has a very limited capability of regeneration of lost neurons and regaining function after injury. Promoting the migration of young neurons derived from endogenous neural stem cells is a promising approach.

Procedures And Architectures
A8G is a mutant of RADA16 in which the alanine in the middle of the peptide sequence is replaced with glycine. A16G is a mutant of RADA16 in which the terminal alanine residue is replaced with glycine. Molecular dynamics simulations visualized similar self-assembling morphology of A16G. N-cadherin plays an important role in the migration of neuroblasts along radial glial fibres in the injured neonatal neocortex. Time-lapse imaging of ventricular-subventricular zone neuroblasts was performed on culture dishes coated with A16G or a mixture of A16G and A16G-Ncad hydrogels. Dcx+ is a marker for neuroblasts observed in the hydrogels after injury. JigSAP is a cell-adhesive fibre-forming peptide with jigsaw-shaped hydrophobic surfaces. JigSAP incorporates JigSAP-tagged vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). AXXXA and GXXXG amino acid sequences are structural motifs found in glycophorin A. These motifs show alpha-helix-to-beta-strand conformational transitions, generating a jigsaw-shaped hydrophobic surface that dimerizes with dovetail packing. JigSAP consists of Ac-RIDARMRADIR-NH2 sequence and shows one-dimensional self-assembly in aqueous media in silico calculated by MD simulation. When JigSAP (1 wt%) is dispersed in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM), circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopic analysis visualizes a conformational change from helical or coil forms to beta-sheet over 100 hours.

Key Results
A16G forms bundled nanofibres and a more robust hydrogel than RADA16. A16G forms curved fibres seen on transmission electron microscopy. The hydrogel made of A16G showed lower stiffness than that of RADA16. The migration rate of neuroblasts was significantly higher on the hydrogel containing A16G-Ncad than on A16G alone. Dcx+ is abundantly observed in the hydrogel of the mixture of A16G and A16G-Ncad. Neuroblasts are seen sparsely in the hydrogels made of A16G alone and a mixture of A16G and Ncad. JigSAP incorporating JigSAP-tagged vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) shows regenerative therapeutic effects in stroke models without cell transplantation. JigSAP forms nanofibres with an average width of 3.2 nm and length of several micrometres. The JigSAP hydrogel exhibits a remarkably high rigidity of 1.1 x 10^4 Pa. The storage modulus G' and loss modulus G EGFP-JigSAP is incorporated at 93 mol%, whereas non-tagged EGFP is incorporated at only 3 mol%. EGFP-5V is incorporated at 66 mol% and EGFP-RADA16 at 55 mol%.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The morphological differences of the fibres could affect the macroscopic properties of the hydrogels. The enhanced mobility with the decreased stiffness and the thixotropic property of A16G hydrogel can be advantageous for injection in biomedical applications. A16G hydrogel containing A16G-Ncad efficiently facilitates the migration of neuroblasts into the injured neocortex in vivo. Fibrous self-assembly of A16G peptide and A16G-Ncad mimics both the structure and dynamic function of intrinsic scaffold cells. The incorporation and releasing property of JigSAP demonstrates wide applicability to controlled sustained release of various full-length growth factors. The JigSAP hydrogel shows more efficient long-term release of the incorporated peptide-tagged proteins than the hydrogels consisting of other self-assembling peptides. The phase transition from gel to sol is useful for drug and cargo release. The self-assembling approach of Chol-MBP is thus advantageous for stabilizing the bicelle morphology to enable prolonged circulation in the blood vessel relative to the spherical vesicles. The membrane-expanding molecular machine AzoMEx functionalizes GUV for endocytosis-like fission, which is useful for encapsulation and delivery of biomacromolecules. These supramolecular approaches to mimicking and controlling bio-interfaces present powerful ways to develop unprecedented regenerative medicines and drug delivery systems.

Contradictions And Limitations
The paper is a Feature Article reviewing recent studies rather than a single experimental study, so specific quantitative results are illustrative rather than from one controlled experiment. The materials science to reconstruct biomimetic interfaces with a dynamic nature is still in its infancy and is expected to make significant progress in the future toward biomedical applications.

Claims
Self-assembling peptide hydrogels can mimic the structure and dynamic function of intrinsic scaffold cells to enhance neuronal migration after brain injury. The migration rate of neuroblasts was significantly higher on the hydrogel containing A16G-Ncad than on A16G alone. Dcx+ is abundantly observed in the hydrogel of the mixture of A16G and A16G-Ncad. A16G hydrogel containing A16G-Ncad efficiently facilitates the migration of neuroblasts into the injured neocortex in vivo. Fibrous self-assembly of A16G peptide and A16G-Ncad mimics both the structure and dynamic function of intrinsic scaffold cells. Neuroblasts are seen sparsely in the hydrogels made of A16G alone and a mixture of A16G and Ncad. This study demonstrates that fibrous self-assembly of A16G peptide and A16G-Ncad mimics both the structure and dynamic function of intrinsic scaffold cells, providing a novel strategy for neuro-regenerative therapy.
Peptide fibres can incorporate and release growth factors for neural tissue regeneration. EGFP-JigSAP is incorporated at 93 mol%, whereas non-tagged EGFP is incorporated at only 3 mol%. The JigSAP hydrogel shows more efficient long-term release of the incorporated peptide-tagged proteins than the hydrogels consisting of other self-assembling peptides. The protein release profile from the gel shows that 21 mol% of EGFP-JigSAP incorporated into the JigSAP nanofibres is released after 24-hour incubation at 37 degrees C. The percentage of released protein increases to 39 mol% after 168 hours of incubation. The release of EGFP-5V and EGFP-RADA16 stagnates after 48 hours of incubation, and only 5 mol% and 8 mol%, respectively, are released even after 168 hours. The incorporation and releasing property of JigSAP demonstrates wide applicability to controlled sustained release of various full-length growth factors, which should be useful as artificial scaffolds for tissue regeneration.
Redox-responsive supramolecular peptide fibres can control cargo release kinetics. The phase transition from gel to sol is useful for drug and cargo release. Met is a redox-active amino acid that is oxidised by reactive oxygen species such as H2O2, producing methionine sulfoxide (MetO). Upon addition of 30% H2O2 aq. to the top of the hydrogels, the gel-sol transition is induced. JigSAP-IMI-Ox and JigSAP-MII-Ox remain dispersed in solution under a physiological condition, whereas JigSAP-IMI and JigSAP-MII form hydrogels under the same condition. The control of the response rate is an important issue to coincide with the target biological events.
Stabilized phospholipid nanosheets enable extended blood circulation relative to spherical vesicles. Disk-shaped carriers tend to show longer circulation times and stronger adhesion to microvascular networks than spherical carriers. Cu2+-mediated crosslinking of Chol-MBP significantly improves the stability of DPPC/Chol-MBP nanosheets in the diluted condition. The self-assembling approach of Chol-MBP is thus advantageous for stabilizing the bicelle morphology to enable prolonged circulation in the blood vessel relative to the spherical vesicles. The FL DPPC vesicles were aggregated and clogged, whereas FL DPPC/Chol-MBP/Cu nanosheets were homogeneously dispersed in the blood vessels. The self-assembling approach of Chol-MBP is thus advantageous for stabilizing the bicelle morphology to enable prolonged circulation in the blood vessel relative to the spherical vesicles, demonstrating a suitable carrier to the whole body by blood administration.
A membrane-expanding molecular machine enables endocytosis-like fission for in vivo delivery of viruses. The light-triggered mechanical motion of AzoMEx embedded in a 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DOPC)-based giant unilamellar vesicle can expand the liposomal membrane and induce outside-in fission. M13 phages encapsulated into GUVDOPC/AzoMEx were transiently protected from external environments, keeping their infectivity. The membrane-expanding molecular machine AzoMEx functionalizes GUV for endocytosis-like fission, which is useful for encapsulation and delivery of biomacromolecules. A molecular approach that enables endocytosis-like transport where membrane deformation is synchronized with substance transport remains critically unexplored. The AzoMEx-GUV technology to encapsulate M13 phages for protection from immune cells in the blood could be applied to an in vivo phage display method for selection of peptides that bind to ligands in living bodies.

Key Figures Tables
Fig. 1 shows the typical dynamic functions of the bio-interfaces in cellular activities. Fig. 2a shows the conformational flexibility of peptide fibres can be a critical factor in controlling the stiffness of the hydrogels. Fig. 3a shows the migration rate of neuroblasts was significantly higher on the hydrogel containing A16G-Ncad than on A16G alone. Fig. 4a shows the JigSAP consists of Ac-RIDARMRADIR-NH2 sequence and shows one-dimensional self-assembly in aqueous media in silico calculated by MD simulation. Fig. 4c shows the JigSAP forms nanofibres with an average width of 3.2 nm and length of several micrometres. Fig. 4e shows the JigSAP hydrogel exhibits a remarkably high rigidity of 1.1 x 10^4 Pa. Fig. 4h shows EGFP-JigSAP is incorporated at 93 mol%, whereas non-tagged EGFP is incorporated at only 3 mol%. Fig. 4k shows the protein release profile from the gel shows that 21 mol% of EGFP-JigSAP incorporated into the JigSAP nanofibres is released after 24-hour incubation at 37 degrees C. Fig. 5a shows the redox-active, gelforming peptides with a methionine (Met) residue in different positions can be used to control the kinetics of the stimulus-responsive gel-sol transition. Fig. 6a shows the cholic acid derivative conjugating a metal-binding peptide sequence PHGGGPHGG (Chol-MBP) is designed as a surfactant. Fig. 6c shows the DPPC/Chol-MBP nanosheets dispersion is diluted to 0.2 wt%, spherical aggregates of less than 100 nm in diameter are observed on TEM. Fig. 6f shows the FL DPPC vesicles were aggregated and clogged, whereas FL DPPC/Chol-MBP/Cu nanosheets were homogeneously dispersed in the blood vessels.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the development of bioinspired supramolecular materials that mimic the dynamic actions of biomacromolecules and supramolecular assemblies located at bio-interfaces. 2. The strongest evidence is the demonstration that self-assembling peptide hydrogels can enhance neuronal migration after brain injury. 3. The future path is the reconstruction of biomimetic interfaces with a dynamic nature, which is expected to make significant progress in the future toward biomedical applications.

summary.title: The properties of highly concentrated aqueous CH3COOK/Na binary electrolyte and its use in sodium-ion batteries
summary.authors: Shahid Khalid, Nicolò Pianta, Simone Bonizzoni, Piercarlo Mustarelli, Riccardo Ruffo
summary.executive_summary: This work investigates highly concentrated aqueous binary electrolytes based on potassium acetate (CH3COOK) combined with varying amounts of sodium acetate (CH3COONa), aiming to develop safe, low-cost, and environmentally friendly electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries. The authors motivate their research by highlighting the limitations of conventional lithium-ion batteries, which rely on organic electrolytes with low flashpoints, high viscosities, and thermally unstable salts like LiPF6 that degrade in the presence of moisture. While aqueous electrolytes offer inherent safety and environmental benefits, they suffer from a narrow thermodynamic electrochemical stability window (ESW) of water (1.23 V), which can only be kinetically extended to about 1.5 V in diluted solutions. To overcome this limitation, researchers have explored high-concentration regimes, culminating in the concept of water-in-salt electrolytes (WISE), where low water activity enables wider voltage windows. However, fluorinated salts commonly used in WISE systems are toxic, expensive, and scarce, prompting the search for cost-effective alternatives like acetate salts. The authors prepare four binary electrolytes with constant 20 mol kg⁻¹ CH3COOK and varying CH3COONa concentrations (1, 2.5, 5, and 7 mol kg⁻¹), along with a 1 M NaAc reference. They characterize the thermal, rheological, transport, and electrochemical properties of these solutions, finding that the most concentrated electrolyte (7N20K) offers the best compromise between conductivity (21.2 mS cm⁻¹ at 25°C) and electrochemical stability (up to 3 V). As a proof of concept, they demonstrate the use of this electrolyte with a carbon-coated LiTi2(PO4)3 (NASICON) electrode, which reversibly inserts and de-inserts Na⁺ ions at about -0.7 V vs. SHE, achieving a first-cycle anodic capacity of 85 mAh g⁻¹, 96% average charge efficiency at low current, and 90% capacity retention after 60 cycles. The excellent interfacial kinetics are evidenced by a low charge-transfer activation energy of 0.12 eV. These results support the feasibility of designing alkaline-ion rechargeable batteries using the water-in-salt approach with safe, abundant acetate-based electrolytes.

Research Context
Super-concentrated aqueous electrolytes are attracting interest for safer, cheaper batteries. Conventional lithium-ion batteries suffer from safety and cost issues. Organic electrolytes have low flashpoints and high viscosities. LiPF6 degrades in moisture, producing HF and corrosion. Aqueous electrolytes have a narrow water stability window of 1.23 V. Diluted aqueous systems can only reach about 1.5 V stability. Water-in-salt electrolytes enable wider voltage windows via low water activity. Fluorinated salts are toxic, expensive, and scarce. Acetate salts are cost-effective, soluble, and abundant alternatives. NASICON materials are ideal electrodes due to stable structure and large channels.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether acetate-based WISE electrolytes can support sodium-ion batteries. The authors hypothesize that increasing NaAc concentration improves electrochemical stability. They predict that 7N20K offers the best balance of transport and stability. They expect good conductivity despite high concentration. They anticipate wide stability window in ideal conditions. They predict reversible Na⁺ insertion in NASICON at about -0.7 V. They expect high charge efficiency and capacity retention. They hypothesize low charge-transfer activation energy for good kinetics.

Methodological Details
NaAc and KAc were purchased at 99% purity from Alfa Aesar. Milli-Q water with conductivity of 6.7 µS cm⁻¹ was used as solvent. Four binary electrolytes were prepared with constant 20 mol kg⁻¹ KAc. The four electrolytes are 1N20K, 2.5N20K, 5N20K, and 7N20K. A 1 M NaAc solution was prepared for comparison. Electrolytes were stored and used at room conditions. Compositional parameters are listed in Table 1. CLTP was synthesized via one-pot sol-gel route. Ammonium dihydrogen phosphate was used as phosphate precursor. Titanium was sourced from titanium butoxide. Lithium acetate dihydrate was used as lithium source. Glucose was used as carbon source.

Procedures And Architectures
The mixture was stirred for 4 h at 55°C in a sealed container. The system was opened and heated to 80°C to remove ethanol. The precursor was dried under vacuum at 100°C. The powder was calcined at 800°C for 6 h under argon. The ramp rate was set to 5°C min⁻¹ with gas flow of 50 ml min⁻¹. Pristine LTP was synthesized via the same route without glucose. XRD was performed using Rigaku Miniflex 600 with Cu cathode. XRD analysis covered 2θ range from 10° to 80° with step size of 0.02. SEM was done using Zeiss Gemini SEM 450. Viscosity was measured with MCR Rheometer 102 using parallel plate. Shear rates ranged from 10 to 300 s⁻¹ at temperatures 10-40°C. DSC was performed using DSC 1Star with Mettler Toledo.

Key Results
Tg increases with salt concentration, indicating salt-in-water to water-in-salt transition. 1N20K and 2.5N20K did not show cold crystallization or melting endotherm. 5N20K and 7N20K showed cold crystallization at -28.06°C and -33.70°C. Melting endotherms were recorded for 5N20K and 7N20K around 0°C. All compositions follow Vogel-Tamman-Fulcher behavior. Ionic conductivity decreases with increasing concentration. 7N20K exhibits conductivity of 21.2 mS cm⁻¹ at 25°C. Viscosity increases with concentration, following Arrhenius behavior. Acetate salts behave as structure-making salts. All electrolytes behave like Newtonian fluids. All electrolytes are classified as quasi-ideal electrolytes. 7N20K follows Kohlrausch's law of strong electrolytes.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The Tg shift indicates growing interactions among solution species. Low liquidus temperature prevents premature cell failure. Conductivity decrease is related to Tg shift and increased viscosity. Strong ion-water interactions suggest formation of water-salt structures. Anions interact with cations without significant reassociation. Cathodic stability increase confirms hydrogen evolution suppression. Anodic ESW expansion is less significant than cathodic. Low charge-transfer activation energy proves good interfacial kinetics.

Contradictions And Limitations
The LSV procedure may overestimate decomposition limits. The procedure involves a large amount of electrolyte. The procedure uses a quasi-ideal electrocatalytic electrode with small surface area. The stability window is only achieved in ideal conditions. Ideal conditions require flooded cell and highly electrocatalytic electrode.

Claims
Highly concentrated aqueous acetate electrolytes can support sodium-ion batteries with good performance. The 7N20K electrolyte shows good conductivity. The 7N20K electrolyte shows wide stability window. The NASICON electrode reversibly inserts Na⁺ ions. The first cycle anodic capacity is 85 mAh g⁻¹. The average charge efficiency is 96% at low current. The capacity retention is 90% after 60 cycles. The stability window is only achieved in ideal conditions. The procedure may overestimate decomposition limits. The results support the feasibility of alkaline-ion batteries. The acetate electrolytes are safe, low-cost, and environmentally friendly. The NASICON electrode is a promising anode material.
The 7N20K electrolyte offers the best compromise between transport properties and electrochemical stability. The 7N20K electrolyte shows good conductivity. The 7N20K electrolyte shows wide stability window. The 7N20K electrolyte has low liquidus temperature. The stability window is only achieved in ideal conditions. The procedure may overestimate decomposition limits. The 7N20K electrolyte is suitable for sodium-ion batteries. The 7N20K electrolyte prevents premature cell failure.

Data And Code Availability
The supporting information is available free of charge. The supporting information includes shear stress vs shear rate curves. The supporting information includes XRPD patterns and SEM images. The supporting information includes additional electrochemical characterization.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The 1 M NaAc solution was used for comparison. The CLTP electrode was compared with pristine LTP. The CLTP electrode was tested in 7N20K and 1 M NaAc. The performance in WISE electrolyte is better than diluted solution.

summary.title: Estimating the size of the solution space of metabolic networks
summary.authors: Alfredo Braunstein, Roberto Mulet, Andrea Pagnani
summary.field_subfield: Statistical physics applied to systems biology / metabolic network analysis
summary.type_of_paper: Methodological (novel algorithm) with empirical validation on real metabolic networks

Executive Summary
This paper introduces a novel, efficient algorithmic strategy for characterizing the entire set of stable flux distributions compatible with the stoichiometric constraints of a metabolic network, without assuming that the cell optimizes an objective function (as Flux Balance Analysis does). The authors frame the feasible flux space as a convex polytope Π embedded in an (N−M)-dimensional affine subspace V, and they aim to compute its volume and the volumes of subspaces, which encode the entropy and marginal distributions of reaction fluxes. The central technical contribution is the use of Belief Propagation (BP), derived from statistical physics and information theory, to compute these sub-dimensional volumes in polynomial time, exploiting the sparsity and locally tree-like structure of real metabolic networks. The method is validated against exact algorithms (LRS, based on reverse search) on low-dimensional random diluted stoichiometric matrices, where it agrees well while scaling almost linearly instead of exponentially. It reproduces Monte Carlo flux distributions for the Red Blood Cell network in minutes versus a week of computation, and it analyzes the E-Coli network, revealing power-law distributions of average fluxes and identifying that gene knock-outs of low-redundancy reactions (e.g., in glycolysis and the Krebs cycle) have the largest impact on the size of the solution space. The work demonstrates that global functional properties of metabolism can be studied efficiently for large biological systems where exact methods fail.

Research Context
Metabolic networks are large and their global function is hard to comprehend. Topological properties are known, but global functional behavior is not. FBA assumes optimization, which only holds under specific conditions. Optimization assumptions fail for knockouts or non-evolved strains. Characterizing the whole solution space has remained elusive. Prior methods relied on expensive Monte Carlo sampling. Monte Carlo sampling is too expensive for large networks.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can the whole set of stable fluxes be characterized efficiently without assuming optimization? Can Belief Propagation compute polytope volumes in polynomial time? Will BP agree with exact algorithms on low-dimensional systems? Will BP match Monte Carlo estimates on the Red Blood Cell network? Do knock-outs of low-redundancy reactions most affect the solution space? Is the flux distribution power-law shaped and thresholded by flux magnitude? Will BP scale polynomially where exact methods explode?

Methodological Details
The study proposes a novel algorithm for estimating solution space size. The authors are from ISI Foundation, University of Havana, and Politecnico di Torino. Metabolic networks are modeled via the mass balance equation. Steady state sets the left-hand side of the balance equation to zero. The steady state is described by the linear system S·ν = o−i ≡ b. The stoichiometric matrix is assumed to have full row rank. The solution subspace is (N−M)-dimensional. Flux positivity and maximal fluxes bound the feasible space. The feasible space is a convex polytope Π in affine space V. The study uses a linear parameterization φ from RN−M to V. The Jacobian determinant λ defines the induced measure on V. The polytope volume is expressed as an integral over V.

Procedures And Architectures
The feasible flux space is formulated in a probabilistic framework. The probability density is uniform over the polytope. Marginal flux probabilities are obtained by integrating out other fluxes. The Bethe approximation expresses P(ν) as a product of marginals. The entropy is expressed in terms of flux marginals. The metabolic problem is cast as a bipartite factor graph. BP messages are exchanged between variable and factor nodes. The message update equations are solved iteratively. Marginals are computed as products of incoming messages. A recursion speeds up the convolution in the message update. The recursion scales as a sum rather than a product. Fourier transforms further accelerate large-degree computations.

Key Results
LRS and BP entropies agree on low-dimensional systems. BP quality improves with finer binning. BP converges as qmax increases toward 1024. BP outperforms LRS beyond N≈12. BP keeps polynomial behavior up to N=120. The Red Blood Cell network has 46 reactions and 34 metabolites. BP distributions match Monte Carlo distributions. BP converged in minutes versus a week for Monte Carlo. The E-Coli network was reduced to 1005 reactions and 560 metabolites. Average fluxes follow a power law with exponent near 1. Jumps appear at ν≈0.5, 0.4, and 0.6. The central metabolism has 40 metabolites, 74 internal reactions, and 10 external fluxes.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The volume encodes the number of feasible steady states. Marginal distributions reveal average flux behavior. The power law reflects network structure. The threshold at ν≈0.6 separates flux regimes. Low-redundancy reactions most affect solution space size. BP is justified by the locally tree-like structure. The method enables analysis of large biological systems.

Contradictions And Limitations
The BP approximation is exact only on trees. BP accuracy depends on discretization. Exact scaling analysis was not possible. Fractional stoichiometric indexes were excluded. Highly connected metabolites were removed. Knock-outs were assumed independent. The meaning of flux jumps is unresolved. The maximum fluxes were set uniformly to 1. The current method handles only linear constraints.

Claims
Belief Propagation efficiently estimates the volume and shape of the feasible flux polytope in polynomial time. The algorithm computes volumes in polynomial time. BP maintains almost-linear running time. The recursion reduces computational cost. Large networks were simulated quickly. Exact methods scale exponentially. BP is approximate, not exact. Scaling analysis was not feasible. Large metabolic networks become tractable. The method outperforms exact algorithms. The approach can be extended to nonlinear constraints.
The feasible flux distributions can be characterized without assuming cellular optimization. The method does not assume extremization. The whole solution space is characterized. FBA relies on optimization assumptions. Optimization holds under specific conditions. Knockouts do not optimize. Global functional behavior becomes accessible. Phenotypic states can be enumerated. The method applies broadly.
Reactions with low topological redundancy most affect the size of the solution space upon knock-out. Low-redundancy reactions have more impact. Glycolysis and Krebs reactions dominate. Entropy change identifies critical reactions. Most reactions have small impact. The independence assumption is violated. Network structure predicts robustness. Flux magnitude correlates with impact. Knock-out effects are predictable.

Data And Code Availability
The study uses published stoichiometric matrices. The E-Coli network was taken from a public database. The exact algorithm LRS is publicly available. The authors equally contributed to this work.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
BP accuracy improves with finer binning. BP converges as discretization increases. The refinement strategy accelerates convergence. Fourier transforms reduce message computation. Removing cofactors improves sparsity. Removing high-connectivity metabolites helps.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1.1 shows running time versus number of fluxes. Figure 1.2 shows BP quality versus binning. Figure 1.3 shows Red Blood Cell flux distributions. Figure 1.4 shows the E-Coli average flux distribution. Figure 1.5 shows the integrated distribution function. Figure 1.6 shows entropy changes for knock-outs. Figure 1.7 shows correlations between entropy and flux.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution. 2. The strongest evidence. 3. The future path.

summary.title: Impact of Chronic Total Occlusion Lesion Length on Six-month Angiographic and 2-year Clinical Outcomes
summary.authors: Jihun Ahn; Byounggeol Choi; Yeon Choi; Jae Kyeong Byun; Ahmed Mashaly; Kareem Abdelshafi; Yoonjee Park; Young Jang; Woohyeun Kim; Eunjin Park; Jin Oh Na; Cheol Ung Choi; Eungju Kim; Chang Gyu Park; Hongseog Seo; Dongjoo Oh; Jinsu Byeon; Sangho Park; Hyeyon Yu; Seung-Woon W Rha
summary.executive_summary: This prospective single-center cohort study investigated whether chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion length influences six-month angiographic and two-year clinical outcomes after successful drug-eluting stent (DES)–based percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). A total of 235 consecutive patients who underwent successful CTO PCI with DES from November 2004 to October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital were divided into a long CTO group (angiographic lesion length ≥30 mm, n=159) and a short CTO group (<30 mm, n=76). Baseline characteristics were largely similar, with prior PCI more frequent in the long CTO group and bifurcation lesions more frequent in the short CTO group; in-hospital intimal dissection was more frequent in the long CTO group. Angiographic follow-up at 6–12 months was obtained in 99 of 159 long CTO patients (62%) and 45 of 76 short CTO patients (59%), and six-month angiographic outcomes—including binary restenosis, in-stent restenosis, late loss, and mean diameter stenosis—were statistically similar between groups, though binary restenosis showed a numerically higher trend in the long CTO group (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.12). Over two years, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; 21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13), total death (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43), cardiac death (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45), and myocardial infarction (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71) did not differ between groups. However, repeat PCI was significantly higher in the long CTO group (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05), predominantly as target vessel revascularization (TVR; 16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified long CTO as an independent predictor of repeat PCI (OR 4.26, CI 1.53–11.9, p=0.006) and TVR (OR 4.23, CI 1.52–11.8, p<0.05). The authors conclude that, despite successful DES-based CTO PCI, long CTO lesions are associated with a higher rate of repeat revascularization, although this did not translate into differences in hard clinical endpoints such as mortality or cardiac death. The study acknowledges limitations including its non-randomized single-center design, small sample size, lack of routine follow-up angiography, and insufficient follow-up duration, and calls for larger long-term studies. This work contributes to the understanding of lesion-length–related prognostic factors in the DES era and supports continued attention to long CTO lesions as a predictor of repeat revascularization, while noting that the absence of differences in hard endpoints may reflect reduced myocardial viability and collateral development in long CTO lesions.

Research Context
Successful CTO PCI is associated with improved clinical outcomes compared with failed CTO PCI. DES and device development have reduced restenosis and adverse events after PCI. Long coronary artery lesions are a worse prognostic factor after PCI. CTO procedural success rates remain lower than non-CTO patients. CTO long-term outcomes are affected by clinical risk factors and baseline lesion characteristics. Lesion length is a major predictor of MACE and restenosis after DES stent implantation. There are no definite answers regarding CTO PCI outcomes according to CTO lesion length, especially in the DES era.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question concerns whether CTO lesion length impacts six-month angiographic and two-year clinical outcomes after successful CTO PCI. The primary hypothesis was that long CTO lesions would be associated with worse angiographic and clinical outcomes due to worse baseline risk factors. The authors hypothesized that the long CTO group has worse clinical risk factors such as prior MI and PCI. The authors hypothesized that newer-generation DES use was dominant in the short CTO group. The authors predicted that paclitaxel-eluting stents were frequently used in the long CTO group. The predicted outcome was that long CTO lesions would predict higher repeat revascularization.

Methodological Details
The study enrolled 235 consecutive CTO patients who underwent successful PCI with DES. Patients were enrolled from November 2004 to October 2010 at Korea University Guro Hospital. The study was conducted at the Cardiovascular Center of Korea University Guro Hospital in Seoul, South Korea. Patients were divided into long CTO (≥30 mm) and short CTO (<30 mm) groups by lesion length. The long CTO group comprised 159 patients with angiographic lesion length ≥30 mm. The short CTO group comprised 76 patients with angiographic lesion length <30 mm. The study protocol was approved by the institutional review board at Korea University Guro Hospital. All patients provided informed consent to participate in the study. CTO was defined as complete coronary obstruction with TIMI flow grade 0 and estimated duration ≥3 months. Only de novo lesions were included, and CTO due to in-stent restenosis was excluded. Loading doses of clopidogrel (300–600 mg) and aspirin (200–300 mg) were administered before the index procedure. Maintenance dual antiplatelet therapy comprised aspirin (100 mg) and clopidogrel (75 mg).

Procedures And Architectures
PCI procedures were performed with current guidelines using standard techniques. Various guidewires were used to cross the CTO lesion. Atheroablative devices were not utilized in the procedures. Mostly simple pre-dilation with balloon was performed to accommodate the stent. All PCI was performed using DES, with the DES type decided by the operator. Procedural success was defined as final diameter stenosis <30% and TIMI grade ≥2. QCA parameters were measured before PCI, immediately after PCI, and 6 months after the procedure. The primary angiographic endpoint was binary restenosis at 6–12 months. Secondary angiographic endpoints included ISR, mean diameter stenosis, MLD, and late loss at 6 months. Two-year follow-up data were collected by face-to-face interview, medical record review, and/or telephone contact. The primary clinical endpoint was MACE, defined as total death, recurrent MI, and revascularization. Secondary clinical endpoints included death, MI, repeat PCI, TLR, TVR, and non-TVR.

Key Results
A total of 235 CTO patients were divided into long CTO (n=159) and short CTO (n=76) groups. Prior PCI was more frequent in the long CTO group than the short CTO group. Bifurcation lesions were more frequent in the short CTO group than the long CTO group. Intimal dissection was more frequent in the long CTO group than the short CTO group. Angiographic follow-up at 6–12 months was obtained in 99 of 159 long CTO patients (62%). Angiographic follow-up at 6–12 months was obtained in 45 of 76 short CTO patients (59%). The incidence of ISR was 33.3% in the long CTO group versus 26.6% in the short CTO group (p=0.42). The incidence of binary restenosis was 19.1% in the long CTO group versus 8.8% in the short CTO group (p=0.12). Late loss was 0.65 ± 0.82 mm in the long CTO group versus 0.46 ± 0.56 mm in the short CTO group (p=0.13). Total death was 3.1% in the long CTO group versus 5.2% in the short CTO group (p=0.43). Cardiac death was 1.2% in the long CTO group versus 2.6% in the short CTO group (p=0.45). Myocardial infarction was 1.8% in the long CTO group versus 2.6% in the short CTO group (p=0.71).

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The higher incidence of repeat PCI and TVR in the long CTO group did not translate into differences in hard endpoints such as mortality. The long CTO group showed numerically higher binary restenosis (19.1% vs. 8.8%, p=0.118). The presence of less myocardial viability and collateral channels may lessen the harmful physiologic effect of restenosis. Long CTO was an independent predictor of repeat PCI (OR 4.26, CI 1.53–11.9, p=0.006). Long CTO was an independent predictor of TVR (OR 4.23, CI 1.52–11.8, p<0.05). The higher incidence of repeat PCI and TVR supports the hypothesis of higher restenosis in long CTO lesions over time.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study was not a randomized study and was a single-center registry with prospectively collected data. Baseline clinical, lesion, and procedural characteristics were slightly different between the two groups. Newer-generation DES use was frequent in the short CTO group, and first-generation stents were frequent in the long CTO group. Follow-up coronary angiography was not routinely performed in all patients. The sample size was relatively small, limiting power to detect differences in angiographic events. The two-year follow-up period was not long enough to evaluate long-term safety and efficacy. Unmeasured confounders and analytical bias could remain despite strict statistical adjustment. Well-developed collaterals and myocardial viability could influence ischemic symptoms and confounders.

Claims
Long CTO lesions are associated with a higher incidence of repeat PCI and TVR after successful DES-based CTO PCI, but this does not translate into differences in hard clinical endpoints such as mortality or cardiac death. Repeat PCI was significantly higher in the long CTO group (18.8% vs. 7.8%, p<0.05). TVR was significantly higher in the long CTO group (16.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.05). Long CTO was an independent predictor of repeat PCI (OR 4.26, CI 1.53–11.9, p=0.006). Long CTO was an independent predictor of TVR (OR 4.23, CI 1.52–11.8, p<0.05). MACE did not differ between groups (21.3% vs. 13.1%, p=0.13). Total death did not differ between groups (3.1% vs. 5.2%, p=0.43). Cardiac death did not differ between groups (1.2% vs. 2.6%, p=0.45). MI did not differ between groups (1.8% vs. 2.6%, p=0.71). Long CTO lesions should be considered a predictor of repeat revascularization in the DES era. The higher TVR incidence did not translate into individual critical hard endpoints such as mortality. Less myocardial viability and collateral channels may lessen the harmful physiologic effect of restenosis. Larger long-term studies are required to reach a final conclusion.
Successful CTO PCI with DES is similarly safe between long and short CTO lesions, with no significant differences in in-hospital complications except intimal dissection. In-hospital complications were similar between the two groups except intimal dissection. Intimal dissection was more frequent in the long CTO group. Procedural safety and efficacy were similar between the two groups during hospitalization. The long CTO group had more frequent intimal dissection, suggesting more complex recanalization. The long CTO group had more frequent false channel wire passage. Long CTO PCI is similarly safe as short CTO PCI despite successful DES implantation. Intimal dissection may reflect more aggressive recanalization in long CTO lesions.

Data And Code Availability
The study data were collected prospectively at Korea University Guro Hospital.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Multivariate logistic regression identified long CTO as an independent predictor of repeat PCI. The analysis adjusted for sex, age, hypertension, DM, chronic kidney disease, prior PCI, and bifurcation lesion. The six-month angiographic outcomes were statistically similar between the two groups.

The study protocol was approved by the institutional review board at Korea University Guro Hospital. All patients provided informed consent to participate in the study. The paper is a bioRxiv preprint not certified by peer review. The paper is available under a CC-BY 4.0 International license.

Key Figures Tables
Table 1 demonstrates baseline clinical and angiographic characteristics of the two groups. Table 2 shows procedural and in-hospital complications, with intimal dissection more frequent in the long CTO group. Table 3 summarizes clinical outcomes for the 2-year follow-up period. Table 4 shows predictors for repeat PCI and TVR, with long CTO as an independent predictor. Table 5 presents six-month angiographic outcomes, with binary restenosis higher in the long CTO group.

1. The core contribution is that long CTO lesions predict higher repeat PCI and TVR after successful DES-based CTO PCI. 2. The future path is larger long-term studies with routine follow-up angiography to reach a final conclusion.

summary.title: Frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions in TbB4
summary.authors: T. Inami, K. Ohwada, Y. H. Matsuda, Z. W. Ouyang, H. Nojiri, D. Okuyama, T. Matsumura, and Y. Murakami
summary.field_subfield: Condensed matter physics; magnetic materials and magnetism
summary.executive_summary: This letter reports resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction (RMXD) experiments on the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice rare-earth tetra-boride TbB4, performed under strong pulsed magnetic fields up to 29 T at the SPring-8 BL22XU undulator beamline. The central motivation is that TbB4 exhibits a multi-step magnetization process above 16 T when the field is applied along the c-axis, yet this curve is difficult to predict because TbB4 has an XY-type ground state. The authors observed the intensity of the (100) magnetic reflection as a function of field and found that the magnetization plateau phases are accompanied by large in-plane (XY) components of the magnetic moments, contrary to the usual expectation that plateau phases contain only moments parallel or antiparallel to the field. A simple spin model is then deduced and used to calculate the magnetization curve. The model assumes an XY ground state with in-plane anisotropy E and excited Ising spins with energy gap D, and reproduces the one-half magnetization plateau. The key theoretical insight is that frustration lifts the degeneracy at the critical fields and creates the observed multi-step metamagnetic behavior, so that frustration is the key to understanding the transitions. The work integrates RMXD using brilliant third-generation synchrotron radiation with pulsed-magnetic-field techniques to explore magnetic structures at high fields close to 30 T. The study concludes that frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions are a general mechanism, common to TbB4 and the previously reported CsFeCl3, even though the spin models for the two magnets are quite different. The paper emphasizes that the integration of two advanced experimental techniques enables exploration of magnetic structures at high fields near 30 T, which will be widely applied in the near future to the high-field phases of many interesting magnets. The research context draws on prior work on magnetization plateaus in Ising antiferromagnets, Heisenberg spins, isolated dimers, and geometrically frustrated Heisenberg antiferromagnets, all of which share the feature that plateau phases have collinear magnetic structures with no ordered moment perpendicular to the field. The novelty of TbB4 is that its plateau phases contain ordered perpendicular components, making it a rare class of magnets characterized by ordered perpendicular components in the plateau phase. The methodological details describe the single crystals grown by the floating zone method, the pulsed magnet with a 0.6 ms pulse duration, the avalanche photodiode detector with a 10 microsecond resolution, and the estimation of the true sample temperature by measuring the temperature dependence of the magnetic peak intensity. The procedures and architectures describe the spin Hamiltonian, the finite-size cells with periodic boundary conditions, the parameter sets J1 = 2, J2 = 1, J3 = 2, D = 1, and the limit E to infinity. The key results report that the net diffraction intensity is about 2x10^5 counts/s, the one-half magnetization plateau is visible between 20 and 24 T, the diffracted intensity of the one-half plateau structure is about one-quarter of the ground state, and the observed intensity is about 30 to 50% of the intensity at 0 T. The interpretation and theoretical implications argue that the plateau phases consist of very hard XY-type magnetic moments and Ising-like magnetic moments, and that frustration lifts the degeneracy at the critical fields. The contradictions and limitations note that the proposed spin model is very much simplified, that interactions further than J3 must be included to account for the splitting at Hc1, and that the model captures basic features but is simplified. The claims section states that the plateau phases include the (100) component, that the large (100) component consists of the ab-plane components, and that frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions are a general mechanism. The data and code availability note that the data are an average of 30 field-scans, and the robustness and ablation notes mention that similar results were obtained with other sets of parameters and different cell sizes. The ethical considerations note that the sample surface was locally heated by irradiation of synchrotron x-rays, and the true sample temperature was estimated. The key figures and tables describe Figure 1, Figure 2, Figure 3, and Figure 4. The top influential citations include the Shastry-Sutherland lattice paper, the resonant anomalous x-ray scattering book, and the pulsed-field x-ray diffraction paper. The three takeaways highlight the core contribution, the strongest evidence, and the future path.

Research Context
Magnetization plateaus are a hallmark of several magnetic materials, where magnetization keeps a constant value at a finite range of magnetic fields. The zero compressibility of plateaus is ascribed to the fact that Sz is a good quantum number, while a variety of mechanisms give rise to plateaus. Ising antiferromagnets exhibit the most comprehensible easy-axis magnetization, such as the one-third magnetization plateau of CoCl2·2H2O. Multi-step magnetization curves of PrCo2Si2 and CeSb are also classified into the Ising category. Magnetization plateaus are observed not only for Ising spins but also for Heisenberg spins, including isolated dimers. Cs3Cr2Cl9 and Ba3Mn2O8 exhibit three-step and two-step magnetization curves, respectively, for S=3/2 and S=1 dimers. In SrCu2(BO3)2, superstructures of excited triplet dimers are stabilized and one-eighth, one-fourth, and one-third plateaus are observed. Geometrically frustrated Heisenberg antiferromagnets also frequently exhibit magnetization plateaus, such as triangular- and pyrochlore-lattice antiferromagnets. For triangular- and pyrochlore-lattice antiferromagnets, one-third and one-half plateaus are observed, respectively. In real magnets, additional mechanisms stabilize the plateau phase, such as four-spin exchange coupling, quantum fluctuations, single-ion anisotropy, and magnetoelastic coupling. A crucial point is that all plateau phases have a collinear magnetic structure, with no ordered magnetic moment perpendicular to the magnetic field. Recently, a multi-step magnetization curve was observed in TbB4, which resembles none of the above-mentioned magnets.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is whether the multi-step magnetization process of TbB4 can be understood, given that TbB4 has an XY-type ground state. The origin of the multiple successive transitions is not easily understood, because the metamagnetic behavior suggests low-lying Ising excited states just above the XY ground state. The hypothesis is that the magnetization plateau phases are accompanied by large XY components of magnetic moments, contrary to the usual collinear expectation. The predicted outcome is that the plateau phases include the (100) component in their magnetic structures. The hypothesis is that the magnetic structures in the plateau phases consist of very hard XY-type magnetic moments and Ising-like magnetic moments. The predicted outcome is that frustration is the key to understanding the observed multi-step magnetization. The hypothesis is that frustration lifts the degeneracy at the critical fields and creates the observed multi-step metamagnetic behavior. The predicted outcome is that frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions are a general mechanism, common to TbB4 and CsFeCl3.

Methodological Details
The experiments were resonant magnetic x-ray diffraction (RMXD) experiments on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice TbB4. The experiments were carried out under strong pulsed magnetic fields up to 29 T. The experiments were performed at undulator beamline BL22XU at SPring-8. The x-ray energy was tuned to the Tb LIII absorption edge (7.514 keV). Magnetic fields up to 29 T were generated using a small pulsed magnet (20 mm in outer diameter and 24 mm in length). The pulse duration is about 0.6 ms. The magnet is a split-pair, and two windows are prepared for incoming and outgoing x-rays. The magnet and a sample were attached to the cold head of a conventional closed cycle refrigerator. Single crystals of TbB4 were grown by the floating zone method. The scattering plane was horizontal, and the a*axis was in the plane. Magnetic fields were vertical and parallel to the c-axis. A high-counting-rate detector, an avalanche photodiode, was used, and diffraction intensity was measured as a function of time with a typical resolution of 10 microsecond.

The field strength was also monitored as a function of time, and the field dependence of the diffraction intensity was obtained from these two series of data. The sample surface was locally heated by irradiation of synchrotron x-rays. The true sample temperature was estimated by measuring the temperature dependence of the magnetic peak intensity at each irradiation intensity. The spin Hamiltonian is H = sum over m=1,2,3 of Jm (sum over i,j of (Sx_i Sx_j + Sy_i Sy_j) + sum over k,l of sz_k sz_l) - E sum over i of (|Sx_i Sy_i| - 1/2) + D sum over k of (sz_k)^2 - g mu_B Hz sum over k of sz_k. The spins are unit vector. Magnetization curves were calculated for finite-size cells with periodic boundary conditions. We consider 4 spins in the crystallographic unit cell (1x1 cell). For simplicity, we initially consider the limit E to infinity. We took J1 = 2, J2 = 1, J3 = 2, D = 1. The calculated magnetization curve is shown in Fig. 4(a).

The net diffraction intensity is about 2x10^5 counts/s, which is marginally strong enough for a pulsed-field experiment. The intensity of the (100) reflection appears below TN1 and is constant below TN2. The field dependence of the (100) reflection at 18 K is shown in Fig. 3(c), and the data are an average of 30 field-scans. A considerable amount of the intensity of the (100) reflection remains in the magnetization plateau phases above 16 T. The intensity decreases with increasing magnetic fields above 16 T and keeps a constant value between 20 and 24 T, where the one-half magnetization plateau is observed. The plateau phases include the (100) component in their magnetic structures. The observed large (100) component in the plateau phases consists of the ab-plane components. The one-half magnetization plateau is clearly reproduced, and the diffracted intensity of this structure is about one-quarter of the ground state. The observed intensity is about 30 to 50% of the intensity at 0 T. Similar results were obtained with other sets of parameters and different cell sizes (2x2 and 1x3 cells). A number of states that have various magnetizations are degenerate at the critical fields Hc1/2 and Hc1. When E is finite, the one-third plateau phase reduces its energy, while the one-half plateau phase does not.

The plateau phases consist of very hard XY-type magnetic moments and Ising-like magnetic moments. The frustration nature of the SS lattice lifts the degeneracy at the critical fields and creates the observed multi-step metamagnetic behavior. Frustration is not only an origin of degenerate states, but also breaks degeneracy. The basic scenario that frustration lifts the degeneracy at a metamagnetic transition is common for both TbB4 and CsFeCl3. Frustration-driven successive metamagnetic transitions are a general mechanism. The proposed spin model captures basic features of the real TbB4, even though it is very much simplified. The spin models for TbB4 and CsFeCl3 are quite different, but the basic scenario is common.

Contradictions And Limitations
The proposed spin model is very much simplified, but it is believed to capture basic features of the real TbB4. Interactions further than J3 must be included to account for the splitting at Hc1. The model is simplified, but it reproduces the one-half magnetization plateau. The true sample temperature was estimated, because the sample surface was locally heated by irradiation of synchrotron x-rays. The intensity away from the resonant energy is background, and the net diffraction intensity is about 2x10^5 counts/s, which is marginally strong enough. The technique is still a challenging experiment, but it will be widely applied in the near future.

The magnetization plateau phases of TbB4 are accompanied by large XY components of magnetic moments. The intensity of the (100) reflection remains in the magnetization plateau phases above 16 T. The plateau phases include the (100) component in their magnetic structures. The observed large (100) component in the plateau phases consists of the ab-plane components. It is expected that all the magnetic moments in plateau phases are parallel or antiparallel to the magnetic field. A canted magnetic structure results in a continuous magnetization curve unlike the observed step-like magnetization process. The magnetic structures in the plateau phases consist of very hard XY-type magnetic moments and Ising-like magnetic moments. Frustration is not only an origin of degenerate states, but also breaks degeneracy. The integration of two advanced experimental techniques enables exploration of magnetic structures at high fields close to 30 T.

Ethical Considerations
The sample surface was locally heated by irradiation of synchrotron x-rays, and the true sample temperature was estimated. The experiments were carried out under strong pulsed magnetic fields up to 29 T, which is a challenging experiment.

Figure 1 shows examples of magnetization plateaus: ground states (left) and magnetization plateau phases (right). Figure 2(a) shows the magnetic structure of TbB4 between TN1 and TN2, and Figure 2(b) shows the magnetization process of TbB4. Figure 3(a) shows the incident energy dependence of the (100) reflection, Figure 3(b) shows the temperature dependence, and Figure 3(c) shows the field dependence. summary.title: Can giant planets form by gravitational fragmentation of discs? Radiative hydrodynamic simulations of the inner disc region
summary.authors: D. Stamatellos & A. P. Whitworth
summary.field_subfield: Astrophysics: planetary system and protoplanetary disc formation
summary.executive_summary: This paper investigates whether giant planets can form close to solar-type stars through gravitational fragmentation of protoplanetary discs. Two competing theories of giant planet formation are core accretion and gravitational fragmentation. Core accretion is slow, requiring millions of years, which may exceed the lifetime of circumstellar discs. Gravitational fragmentation is fast, occurring on a dynamical timescale of a few hundred years, but requires two conditions: gravitational instability (Toomre Q < 1) and fast cooling (tCOOL < C(γ) tORB). The authors use radiative hydrodynamic simulations with a newly developed method that accounts for radiative transfer effects, including the equation of state and energy equation, in smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations. They simulate a 0.07 M⊙ disc around a 0.5 M⊙ star, extending from 2 to 40 AU, in two cases: one with a constant background radiation field of 10 K, and one with additional heating from the central star. In both cases, the disc does not fragment. In the first case, the disc cannot cool fast enough (cooling time > 2 tORB). In the second case, the disc is not gravitationally unstable (Q > 1.5). The results corroborate previous studies by Boley et al. (2006) and Cai et al. (2007), who used different radiative transfer treatments. The authors conclude that disc fragmentation is unlikely to produce giant planets around solar-type stars at radii < 50 AU. This work contributes to resolving the contradictory results in the literature about whether disc fragmentation can produce giant planets close to the central star, which stem from different treatments of radiative transfer. The study uses realistic dust opacities and an equation of state that includes the rotational and vibrational degrees of freedom of molecular hydrogen, as well as the chemical states of hydrogen and helium. The simulations are performed using the SPH code dragon, which uses an octal tree to compute gravity and find neighbours, adaptive smoothing lengths, multiple particle timesteps, artificial viscosity with the Balsara switch, and a second-order Runge-Kutta integration scheme. The authors also compare their results with analytic calculations of Hubeny (1990) for the vertical temperature profile of the disc. The study is important because it provides evidence that gravitational fragmentation is not a viable mechanism for forming giant planets close to the central star, which has implications for our understanding of planet formation and the diversity of exoplanets. The authors acknowledge that their results are consistent with previous simulations and analytical calculations, which suggests that the conclusion is robust. However, they also note that fragmentation may be possible at larger radii (> 100 AU), where the cooling times are sufficiently short, but that such objects are unlikely to migrate inwards to become hot Jupiters. The study is limited by the assumption of a constant mean molecular weight and the neglect of metal contributions, which may affect the accuracy of the results. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive investigation of the possibility of giant planet formation by gravitational fragmentation, using state-of-the-art numerical simulations and realistic physical models.

summary.title: Three-dimensional topological valley photonics
summary.authors: Wenhao Li, Qiaolu Chen, Ning Han, Xinrui Li, Fujia Chen, Junyao Wu, Yuang Pan, Yudong Ren, Hongsheng Chen, Haoran Xue, Yihao Yang
summary.field_subfield: Photonics / Topological photonics (optics and wave physics)
summary.executive_summary: Topological valley photonics exploits the valley degree of freedom to control electromagnetic waves, but prior work has been confined to two dimensions, where light confinement along the third dimension is achieved in a non-topological way and suffers from out-of-plane losses, restricting light flow to planar geometries. This paper introduces a three-dimensional (3D) topological valley photonics framework that combines a complete photonic bandgap with vectorial valley-contrasting physics. Unlike 2D systems with a single pair of valleys characterized by scalar valley Chern numbers, the 3D model involves triple pairs of valleys characterized by valley Chern vectors, enabling vectorial bulk valley vortices and canalized chiral valley surface states. The authors develop a 3D photonic crystal with a diamond-like lattice built from perfect electric conductor (PEC) spheres and rods, and break inversion symmetry by using two spheres of different diameters within each face-centered-cubic cell. This gapping produces a complete photonic bandgap and six valleys grouped into three pairs by time-reversal symmetry. Using the k·p method, they derive an effective Hamiltonian near each valley and show that the Berry curvature has nonzero components only in the plane perpendicular to the valley momentum, verifying vectorial valley-contrasting physics. Experimentally, they use a vectorial chiral source array to selectively excite valley states with valley-locked chirality and observe directional outcoupling at 13.8 GHz, confirming valley-momentum locking. They also demonstrate canalized chiral surface states on all surfaces of a shaped sample and reveal a right-hand-thumb rule relating the valley Chern vectors to the circulating propagation direction of the surface states. The findings highlight applications in 3D waveguiding, directional radiation, and imaging, and suggest extension to terahertz and optical frequencies using all-dielectric diamond-like crystals.

summary.title: Mechanochemical synthesis of eco-friendly fertilizer from eggshell (calcite) and KH2PO4
summary.authors: Roger Borges; Amanda Soares Giroto; Rodrigo Klaic; Fernando Wypych; Caue Ribeiro
summary.executive_summary: This study presents an environmentally beneficial and cost-effective method of producing calcium phosphate bioceramics (potassium calcium phosphates) for soil conditioning, based on reverse logistics and green chemistry. The approach uses a free-solvent mechanochemical process between eggshell waste (calcite, CaCO3) and monobasic potassium dihydrogen phosphate (KH2PO4). The resulting K3CaH(PO4)2 and possibly CaKPO4 phases provide better nutrient management of P, K, and Ca when applied to soil systems, where the material first releases K and forms hydroxyapatite, serving as an important P and Ca bioavailable source at pH ~5, which comprises a large part of many countries' soils. Eggshells are important wastes of food industries and excellent CaCO3 sources (more specifically calcite), while millions of tons of eggshells are produced as biowaste around the world, disposed in landfills with no pretreatment and producing odors due to microbial growth. The solid-state mechanochemical activation consists in applying mechanical energy to promote a chemical reaction from solid reagents using mainly friction and impact forces. The process mainly produces K3CaH(PO4)2 and possibly CaKPO4, among other non-crystalline compounds and also CO2 resulting from CaCO3 decomposition. Compared to KH2PO4, all these phosphates may exhibit very different solubility according to the different bonds between different metal cations. The produced potassium calcium phosphates may be classified as smart release fertilizers, since they provide a delay of the bioavailability of P and K and also improve the bioavailability of Ca. The solid-state mechanochemical activation allows the reactions to occur in a solvent-free environment, producing no liquid or solid waste in the process, ensuring huge savings during the production process. The literature reports the mechanochemical synthesis of hydroxyapatite from different precursors, but no mechanochemical process has been reported for the production of K3CaH(PO4)2 and CaKPO4 from calcite provided by eggshell and KH2PO4. The eggshells were collected by the authors in their homes, washed with water and dried at room temperature, presenting a diameter between 1 and 10 mm before the grinding process; the KH2PO4 PA was supplied from Vetec. The milling process was performed with a high-energy ball mill, Fritsch Pulverisette 7, with a 250 ml zirconia bowl, 5 zirconia balls of 15 mm diameter. The essays were performed using the weight ratio of 1:1 (w/w) of eggshell and KH2PO4 for various times and speeds. After milled, the samples were characterized by XRD, NMR MAS, TGA, and DSC. The nutrient content of the samples and precursors were obtained dissolving the samples by using acid digestion in H2SO4/H2O2 PA mixture. The phosphorus diffusion rates in soil were performed in Petri dishes containing moist soil. The kinetic study of the nutrient release was firstly evaluated in citric acid solution (wt 2%) according to the recommended procedure from MAPA. The kinetic study of the nutrient release was also evaluated in soil. The results indicate new phosphate phases such as K3CaH(PO4)2 and KCaPO4, which present in citric acid solution a slower release character of potassium and phosphorus compared to the precursor KH2PO4, and a faster release character compared to the precursor CaCO3 from eggshell. The soil essays performed indicate the same behavior, but a general slower release trend when compared to citric acid solution essays, which can be explained by hydroxyapatite formation. Based on the reverse logistics and green chemistry, this study proposes the use of eggshell and KH2PO4 to design an eco-friendly fertilizer that guarantees a better nutrient management, playing on the solubility of calcium, potassium, and phosphorus. To reach this aim, a mechanochemical process was used, free of solvent, and presenting no unwanted subproduct. The results indicate new phosphate phases such as K3CaH(PO4)2 and KCaPO4, which present in citric acid solution a slower release character of potassium and phosphorus compared to the precursor KH2PO4, and a faster release character compared to the precursor CaCO3 from eggshell. The soil essays performed indicate the same behavior, but a general slower release trend when compared to citric acid solution essays, which can be explained by hydroxyapatite formation, that is still an important source of calcium and phosphorus as a long-term slow release fertilizer.

The milling process was performed with a high-energy ball mill, Fritsch Pulverisette 7, with a 250 ml zirconia bowl, 5 zirconia balls of 15 mm diameter. The essays were performed using the weight ratio of 1:1 (w/w) of eggshell and KH2PO4 for various times and speeds. After milled, the samples were characterized by XRD, NMR MAS, TGA, and DSC. The nutrient content of the samples and precursors were obtained dissolving the samples by using acid digestion in H2SO4/H2O2 PA mixture. The phosphorus diffusion rates in soil were performed in Petri dishes containing moist soil. The kinetic study of the nutrient release was firstly evaluated in citric acid solution (wt 2%) according to the recommended procedure from MAPA. The kinetic study of the nutrient release was also evaluated in soil. The results indicate new phosphate phases such as K3CaH(PO4)2 and KCaPO4, which present in citric acid solution a slower release character of potassium and phosphorus compared to the precursor KH2PO4, and a faster release character compared to the precursor CaCO3 from eggshell. The soil essays performed indicate the same behavior, but a general slower release trend when compared to citric acid solution essays, which can be explained by hydroxyapatite formation. Based on the reverse logistics and green chemistry, this study proposes the use of eggshell and KH2PO4 to design an eco-friendly fertilizer that guarantees a better nutrient management, playing on the solubility of calcium, potassium, and phosphorus. To reach this aim, a mechanochemical process was used, free of solvent, and presenting no unwanted subproduct. The results indicate new phosphate phases such as K3CaH(PO4)2 and KCaPO4, which present in citric acid solution a slower release character of potassium and phosphorus compared to the precursor KH2PO4, and a faster release character compared to the precursor CaCO3 from eggshell. Research Context
Reverse logistics is an instrument of economic and social development characterized by a set of actions, procedures and means to enable the collection and restitution of solid waste to the business sector, for reuse, in its cycle or in other cycles productive, or other environmentally appropriate final destination. An application of this concept is to provide novel processes for the synthesis of different calcium and / or potassium phosphates from any source of calcium carbonate (CaCO3), making it a soil conditioner. Among sources, eggshells are important wastes of food industries and excellent CaCO3 sources (more specifically calcite) (Byeon, 2016), with monobasic potassium dihydrogen phosphate. Everyday millions of tons of eggshells are produced as biowaste around the world, disposed in landfills with no pretreatment and producing odors due to microbial growth. Normally the reactions are processed by solid state mechanochemical activation, to produce different materials concerning physico-chemical features, especially the solubilization and diffusion of its constitutional elements and chemical species. Basically, the solid-state mechanochemical activation consists in applying mechanical energy to promote a chemical reaction (Kouznetsov et al., 2016) from solid reagents using mainly friction and impact forces. The process mechanism involved is still quite complex to evaluate, but the applied energy must be large enough to be able to break the reagent bonds and promote solid phase ion migration, in the case of this study, to form a new structure. The process mainly produces K3CaH(PO4)2 and possibly CaKPO4, among other non-crystalline compounds and also CO2 resulting from CaCO3 decomposition. Compared to KH2PO4, all these phosphates may exhibit very different solubility according to the different bonds between different metal cations. It is influenced by the size of the metal cation and its charge, influencing the reticular energy of the structure (Jenkins et al., 1999). Besides that, the experimental release essays reveal that potassium dihydrogen phosphate exhibits much faster solubilization behavior than calcium or calcium and potassium phosphates. Composed solely of fertilizer components (HPO4 2-/PO4 3-, Ca 2+ and K +) (Liu and Lal, 2015), the produced potassium calcium phosphates may be classified as smart release fertilizers, since they provide a delay of the bioavailability of P and K and also improve the bioavailability of Ca turning these materials an excellent alternative in these nutrient management.

The authors predict that these materials would promote better nutrient management by delaying the bioavailability of phosphorus and potassium (which are highly soluble from KH2PO4) and increasing the calcium bioavailability. The authors predict that in low rotation speeds do not provide enough energy to degrade the total amount of calcite to form calcium potassium phosphates. The study hypothesizes that the new phosphates phases from milling made calcium readily available, while delaying the release of phosphorus and potassium. The authors predict that the slower release for calcium and phosphorus for 2 h/600 rpm sample and the P radial diffusion are probably related to hydroxyapatite formation. The study hypothesizes that hydroxyapatite is an important long-term calcium and phosphorus slow release fertilizer, turning systematically soluble by the natural soil pH acidification, especially under pH 5. Methodological Details
The eggshells were collected by the authors in their homes, washed with water and dried at room temperature, presenting a diameter between 1 and 10 mm before the grinding process. The KH2PO4 PA was supplied from Vetec. The milling process was performed with high-energy ball mill, Fritsch Pulverisette 7, with a 250 ml zirconia bowl, 5 zirconia balls of 15 mm diameter. The essays were performed using the weight ratio of 1:1 (w/w) of eggshell and KH2PO4 were performed firstly for 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 3 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h at 600 rpm, and secondly at 100, 200, 400 and 600 rpm for 2 h. Considering the purity of KH2PO4 and assuming that the eggshells are mainly composed by CaCO3, the mixture corresponds to 0.75 mmol of KH2PO4 and 1 mmol of CaCO3. After milled, the samples were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), nuclear magnetic resonance, magic-angle spinning (NMR) MAS, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The nutrient content of the samples and precursors were obtained dissolving the samples by using acid digestion in H2SO4/H2O2 PA mixture (8:1 v/v, by 24 h at 250 °C), and determined by atomic absorption (K and Ca) and colorimetric (P) methods. Before release essays at citric acid solution (2 wt%), the material has been pelletized to simulated commercial products. The pellets were obtained in steel pelletizer applying the pressure of 5 bar, and the weight was standardized to 100 mg/L of P. One single pellet were used in each essay in triplicate, that was placed in 10 mL beaker, this small beaker was immersed into 300 mL of 2% citric acid solution in a 600 mL beaker, the system was kept closed with polyvinyl chloride (PVC) film, in a constant temperature room at 25 °C and under a magnetic stirring. The stirring ensures homogeneous distribution of diffused elements, and aliquots of 1.2 mL at different times (from 15 min to 30 days) have been collected to evaluate the release behavior and allow the calculation of a release kinetic model of Ca, K and P. The phosphorus diffusion rates in soil were performed in Petri dishes containing moist soil, according to the method described by Degryse and Mclaughlin (2014).

Procedures And Architectures
This method consists to use a pre-treated paper to mark the P diffusion in soil. In each Petri dish with diameter of 8.6 cm, 78 g of dry and sieved 2.0 mm mesh soil were added to achieve the desired density of 1.2 g.cm -3. In order to achieve 70% of the maximum soil water retention capacity, 15 mL deionized water were added. The papers are scanned and analyzed using image software (GNU Image Manipulation Program, v. 2.6.11, Free Software). The scanned images are converted to black-with binary images, using a threshold color value (e.g. on a 0-255 scale), and the area of the high P-zone is quantified using the histogram command. In order to investigate the release behavior closer to real conditions, soil release essays were carried out under aerobic conditions in plastic container containing 50 g of sandy soil (Table S2) with 75% water saturation. The experiments were performed at 3, 7, 15 and 30 days, using a single pellet for each container, the pellet weight was standardized to 300 mg of P per kg of soil. After each release period the solid residues samples were removed from the soil and characterized by XRD; potassium and calcium were extracted from the soil by HCl (0.05 Mol/L) and KCl (1 Mol/L) methods, respectively; and phosphorus was extracted from soil using Mehlich 1 method (Embrapa, 1979). A colorimetric analyses of molybdenum blue was used to quantify phosphorus released content into the solution (Murphy and Riley, 1962) and potassium and calcium released content were quantify by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy (FAAS), with a PerkinElmer PinAAcle 900T instrument, in flame atomization mode. The XRD 6000 diffractometer (Shimadzu) was used with a Cu Kα incident beam (λ = 0.1546 nm) and scanning speed of 2° min -1 at 30 kV voltage and 40 mA current. The relative intensity of the diffraction peaks was registered in the angular range (2θ) of 3-40°. Studies of the crystallization behavior of the precursor and samples were carried out using a TA Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC) (TA Q100 Controller) with refrigerated cooling system (RCS).

The milling process between KH2PO4 and eggshell (98% of CaCO3) performed from 2 h and 400 rpm produce a mixture of phosphates, mainly K3CaH(PO4)2 (PDF database n° 22-1218) and possibly CaKPO4 (PDF database n° 33-1002). Bellow these milling parameters (time and milling speed) only the reactants diffraction patterns are found, i.e., no evidence of chemical reaction is observed. In general, it was noticed that only a minimal energy is required to initiate the mechanochemical reaction, and, as a consequence, the diffraction patterns have huge changes attributed to the formation of different polymorphic potassium calcium phosphate phases. When milling time increases, secondary reactions begin, for example, mechanochemical dehydroxylation of the new formed phosphates. One can propose the non-stoichiometric reaction of the main products, with CaKPO4 more evident after 24 h of milling. The TGA curve of KH2PO4 show two main loss events: since it is an anhydrous material, the moisture loss is not seen and the first step at 200°C should be associated to crystallization water loss. The second step at 300°C corresponds to polycondensation, concomitant with structural water loss. The residual mass (89%) regards to KPO3 formation is consistent to the theoretical (87%) (Fig. 2). The thermal degradation of eggshell has two main steps: a first mass loss step below 300 °C attributed to moisture elimination concomitant with organic membrane degradation; and a second step related to calcite decomposition below 700 °C. The eggshells are mainly composed by CaCO3, as attested by XRD pattern (Fig. 1), which is also confirmed by the small difference from experimental residue (56%) and the theoretical (59%). In the case of milled samples (Fig. 2), three mass loss events are observed: the first step, centered at 280°C, is related to crystallization water loss concomitant with physically adsorbed moisture elimination. The second step, centered at 420°C, is associated to partial structural water loss and structure dimerization, and the final step, centered at 710°C corresponds to final structural water loss reaction and structure polycondensation.
